segments.sub: What if every atom lost just one electron... for ten seconds?
segments.tts: What if every atom lost just one electron... for ten seconds?

segments.sub: Every atom is a tiny balance: a positive nucleus, and negative electrons around it.
segments.tts: Every atom is a tiny balance: a positive nucleus, and negative electrons around it.

segments.sub: Take away one electron, and every atom becomes positive.
segments.tts: Take away one electron, and every atom becomes positive.

segments.sub: And positive charges push each other away. Hard.
segments.tts: And positive charges push each other away. Hard.

segments.sub: First, your skin would tingle, and every hair on your body would stand straight up.
segments.tts: First, your skin would tingle, and every hair on your body would stand straight up.

segments.sub: Huh? Why is my hair floating?
segments.tts: Huh? Why is my hair floating?

segments.sub: Then your body would try to push itself apart, with as much energy as the Sun gives off in a whole minute.
segments.tts: Then your body would try to push itself apart, with as much energy as the Sun gives off in a whole minute.

segments.sub: The ground, the oceans, the entire planet would blast apart from the inside.
segments.tts: The ground, the oceans, the entire planet would blast apart from the inside.

segments.sub: With more energy than a billion billion billion supernovas.
segments.tts: With more energy than a billion billion billion supernovas.

segments.sub: And the ten seconds? They don't matter. It would all be over in a tiny fraction of the very first second.
segments.tts: And the ten seconds? They don't matter. It would all be over in a tiny fraction of the very first second.

segments.sub: So the next time you lose something small... be glad it wasn't an electron.
segments.tts: So the next time you lose something small... be glad it wasn't an electron.
